relhic_mass_tier_tng50_1.analogue: RELHIC / UFD-mass field halos (Cloud-9 host mass is NOT in this tier)

cloud9_mass_anchor_tier_tng50_1.analogue: Cloud-9 host mass (4.1-5.8e9 Msun); see decision D8

control_tier_tng100_1.analogue: resolution control only - EXCLUDED from merger claims

exclusion_reason.control_tier_tng100_1: median 0 tracked mergers; TNG100-1 subhalo trees are tracked only to z ~ 3.5, so absence of a merger is a tracking limit, not a physical quiescence

measured_vs_literature.direction: both measured tiers are MORE active than the assumed 0.5; the Cloud-9-mass tier contains no quiescent halo at all
measured_vs_literature.consequence_for_cloud9_label: HALOS_G2 labels the Cloud-9 host 'quiescent' from observation (Zhou+ 2023). Its TNG50-1 mass analogue is uniformly active. The label stays observational; the tension is recorded as decision D8, not resolved by relabeling.

what_this_does_not_measure: the effect of a merger on a gravothermal collapse time (the 0.7 / 8.0 magnitudes are literature calibration, not measured here)
halo mass above ~6e9 Msun in TNG50-1 resolution-matched form (see D8: no z=0 primary in the 4-6e9 Msun cell reaches V_max >= 30 km/s)
merger mass ratios - the local trees record merger events, not their mass ratio, so 'major merger' in the literature sense is not equivalent to these counts
